significance: Built in 879 by Indravarman I soon after his accession, Preah Ko sets six brick towers in two rows on a single sandstone platform, its sanctuaries honouring three deified male ancestors and their wives in association with Shiva; the front central tower commemorates Jayavarman II, who founded the Khmer empire in 802. The towers were restored in the early 1990s with German government funding.
